searchText: btw testing out our EOF implementation in vyper and due to the RJUMPI / CALLF problems mentioned in dec or january, vyper contract codesize actually gets worse by 3-5% when compiling for EOF target that's interesting, solidity actually got smaller, but maybe they were using all features do you have some example code so we can investigate? which all features? every proposed opcode from december well it's going to be pretty much any code i mean an example input + output for instance instead of being able to JUMPI to a shared revert block, we have to branch and CALLF a shared revert block oh that's why we have JUMPF 🙂 ok maybe i am still misunderstanding the new jumpf semantics does jumpf somehow do branching? no, but it removes the stack balancing restrictions of callf for revert blocks we can't conditionally call a subroutine without branching those opcodes were considered but not implemented ok so anyway like i said, due to stack validation restrictions, code targeting eof actually gets bigger, not smaller and it turns out not to be pathological, i am testing with various real life sample contracts yes that's expected, depends on the cases/compilers/design the first motivation is validation and runtime oriented, code size is secondary
